Article Title: 'Acted of his own volition': ACP Bhagat steps aside from Addl DCP charge amid harassment probe
Article Text:
Amid harassment probe, ACP Bhagat steps aside from Addl DCP charge

NEW DELHI: Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Connaught Place Vivek Bhagat, who was promoted to the rank of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Addl DCP), has sought withdrawal of the order assigning him the post, citing an ongoing inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment.Following his request to step aside pending the inquiry, the Delhi government modified its administrative order assigning the current duty charge of Addl DCP to 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers.Earlier, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu had approved assigning the current duty charge (CDC) of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police to 12 DANIPS officers posted with the Delhi Police with immediate effect. ACP Vivek Bhagat, who is currently serving as SDPO Connaught Place, was among the officers named in the order.The Delhi government later issued a clarification saying the October 5 order was being amended following a formal request from Bhagat."Vivek Bhagat, ACP, of his own volition, has requested not to avail the current duty charge assignment, till a full enquiry has been conducted in the matter of alleged harassment of women journalists and such enquiry has been satisfactorily concluded. Accordingly, the order dated October 5, 2026, as aforesaid, is being modified and will be reissued with respect to assignment of current duty charge on the eleven remaining officers," the Delhi government stated in a post on X.The administration clarified that the assignment is an interim administrative arrangement and does not amount to a regular promotion."As stated in the order, the assignment of current duty charge is a temporary arrangement which confers no financial benefit, and no statutory duties of the regular incumbents can be exercised by the officers to whom current duty charge has been assigned," the statement added.Following Bhagat’s exclusion, a revised order assigning the current duty charge to the remaining 11 DANIPS officers will be issued shortly.Earlier in the day, Bhagat, who has been accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during the October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar, was included in the order assigning the rank of Additional DCP, drawing criticism from various quarters.Three women journalists had accused Delhi Police personnel of sexual harassment during the October 3 protest against alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Delhi Police has received the complaints and forwarded them to the Crime Branch for further inquiry.
Article Summary: Vivek Bhagat, who was promoted to the rank of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Addl DCP), has sought withdrawal of the order assigning him the post. He has been accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during the October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar. The Delhi government later issued a clarification saying the October 5 order was being amended following a formal request.

Article Title: 'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, time to resign': Rahul Gandhi as INDIA bloc march to EC stopped
Article Text:
'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,' Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X

INDIA bloc MPs stopped near Niti Aayog

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday called on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign as INDIA bloc MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission of India headquarters over alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,” Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X as he led the opposition MPs towards the ECI office.The march, which began from Parliament's Makar Dwar around 11 am, was stopped by security personnel near the Niti Aayog office. Several INDIA bloc MPs subsequently sat in protest, with opposition leaders later staging a dharna at Parliament Street.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule were among the opposition leaders participating in the march.Visuals showed Rahul Gandhi leading the march along with several INDIA bloc MPs, who were carrying placards and cutouts of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The opposition MPs were seeking Kumar's removal over alleged irregularities in the SIR process. The INDIA bloc had announced the march from Parliament to Nirvachan Sadan as part of its campaign against the Election Commission's handling of the electoral roll revision.The march was met with heavy security deployment in central Delhi. Barricades were placed along the route and Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed around Transport Bhawan ahead of the protest.After being prevented from proceeding towards the ECI headquarters, several opposition MPs sat in protest near Parliament Street.AAP said it would skip the march, with the party saying it would fight the issue through its own means.Opposition steps up attack over SIRThe protest comes amid an ongoing political confrontation between the opposition and the Election Commission over the SIR exercise and alleged discrepancies in voter rolls.The Supreme Court on Tuesday said it had not approved any modified version of Form 6 used for voter enrolment during the SIR process. CJI Surya Kant said, “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us.”The court issued notices to the Centre, ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and other officials while declining to pass an ex-parte interim order suspending Kumar.Ahead of the march, several opposition leaders criticised the Election Commission's handling of the SIR process. Congress and INDIA bloc leaders have demanded Kumar's removal, while the BJP has rejected the opposition's allegations.Mamata Banerjee has said the protests will continue until Kumar resigns and has also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation.Congress MP Jairam Ramesh had said the march would be peaceful. The opposition has also announced district-level padyatras till October 8 and "Save votes, save the country" rallies from October 25 to November 25.
Article Summary: 'Gyanesh, it’s done, bro, Time to resign,' Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X as he led the opposition MPs towards the ECI office. The march, which began from Parliament's Makar Dwar around 11 am, was stopped by security personnel near the Niti Aayog office.

NEW DELHI: The Punjab government will approach the Supreme Court to challenge the Punjab and Haryana high court’s order directing a CBI probe into the matter concerning three letters written by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the Punjab Director General of Police (DGP), AAP said.The state government will file an appeal against the High Court’s order.The High Court had on Monday directed that the matter be handed over to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) after hearing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Nikhil Thamman. The petition was filed after the Punjab Police allegedly failed to register a case based on the ED’s letters.The ED had sought registration of an FIR against Rajbir Singh Ghumman, Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, and certain other individuals over alleged corruption.During the hearing, Thamman also submitted that Punjab has not had a regular DGP for more than four years. Article Title: 'Country moving in a democratic way': BJP on SC notice to poll body, Centre on pleas against CEC
Article Text:
The SC however refused to pass any interim direction in the matter

NEW DELHI: The ruling BJP on Monday said the Supreme Court's decision to issue notices to the Election Commission (EC) and the Centre on pleas seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar showed that all institutions in the country were "functioning independently" and there was no atmosphere of "fear and dictatorship"."The country is moving in a very democratic way. Everyone is speaking their heart out. All procedures and systems are being followed. Where else could there be a better model of democracy? I feel India is celebrating democracy," BJP MP and spokesperson Sambit Patra told reporters at a news conference at the party headquarters in Delhi when asked about the development.Patra's remarks came after the Supreme Court sought responses from the EC and the Centre within a week on a plea challenging the manner in which the poll panel, led by CEC Gyanesh Kumar, allegedly took decisions without the approval of the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.However, a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to pass any interim order in the matter.The bench observed that it could not pass an order merely on the basis of a media report, which may or may not be accurate. However, it asserted that if any decisions of the EC were found to have been taken unilaterally by the CEC, the Supreme Court could reconsider or recall them."They (EC) are expected to take unanimous decisions. If there is no unanimity, it has to be by majority. If records show some decision was not unanimous, etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra vires. Can we ex parte come to a decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," the CJI said.The controversy stems from an Indian Express report published late last month, which claimed that Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The report alleged that some of these decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation.According to the report, the poll panel's ECINet software added a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR in Form 6, the voter registration form, without the legal amendment required under election rules. The two commissioners reportedly objected to the change.The EC has since restored Form 6 to its original format in states where the SIR has been completed. However, the requirement continues in states and Union territories where the roll revision is still underway.Responding to the Indian Express report, the commission said that "differing views and observations" among its members were a "normal part" of deliberations in any multi-member institution. The EC also stated that all decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously by Kumar and the two Election Commissioners.Meanwhile, Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi upped the ante against Kumar after the Supreme Court clarified that it did not approve any modification made by the EC in Form 6.In a social media post on X, the Congress leader accused the CEC of changing the application citizens use to register as new electors "illegally and unilaterally.""It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP," Rahul Gandhi wrote on X, adding that was now established "beyond doubt" that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 "illegally and unilaterally."He also shared the screenshot of the September 26 Election Commission statement which read -- "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used."
Article Summary: The Supreme Court issued notices to the Election Commission and the Centre on pleas seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to pass any interim order in the matter.

Article Title: BJP drops all 8 Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha members, including Hardeep Puri - what it means
Article Text:
Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma also are among those who have not been renominated.

Cabinet reshuffle on cards?

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday named eight candidates for the Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, dropping all of its outgoing members from the state. Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Union minister of state for consumer affairs BL Verma also are among those who have not been renominated.The nominees, approved by the party's Central Election Committee, are Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar. Voting for 10 UP seats is on October 16, and the last date for filing nominations is October 6.The outgoing BJP members, apart from Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma, are Arun Singh, Neeraj Shekhar, Geeta Shakya, Brijlal and Seema Dwivedi.The eighth seat belonged to former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma, who resigned on September 11 after being appointed lieutenant governor (LG) of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. His term was due to end on November 25, like those of the others.Meanwhile, the move has set the ball rolling for different interpretations ahead of the UP assembly polls and the long speculated Union cabinet reshuffle as no sitting BJP member from the state was retained.Puri's name had been widely discussed for renomination, as had that of former Union minister Smriti Irani, who is also absent from the list.It is seen as a move motivated by the 2027 assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, which the party will contest to form government for the third time in the state. The list, inevitably, appears to have names chosen to balance social, regional and caste combinations.The three candidates in the list are from the upper castes, three from Other Backward Classes (OBC) and two from Scheduled Castes. Ojha and Pandey, both Brahmins, are among the upper-caste picks. Dharampal Singh, a Lodhi, replaces outgoing MP BL Verma, who belongs to the same community. The list also spans Pal and Kurmi communities. Two women, Gangwar and Rawat, are among the nominees.The party seems to have leaned towards grassroots and organisational leaders rather than prominent national faces with the induction of Dharampal Singh, an animal husbandry minister in CM Yogi Adityanath 's government.BJP is learnt to have zeroed in on at least 100 MLAs who are reportedly facing anti-incumbency at the ground level and a large number of them may be denied the ticket to contest the UP Assembly elections next year.Sources said this data has emerged after an on-ground assessment done by the party in 255 seats represented by BJP in the UP Assembly.A top UP BJP member confirmed to TOI that about 100 MLAs are on the radar following reports of lack of trust in them among voters. Friction with the organisational brass at the local level is also being accounted for while flagging these legislators, the senior member said. Sources said that feedback has also been taken from RSS vis-à-vis the candidacy of the sitting MLAs.The BJP's decision not to renominate Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Union minister of state BL Verma has also fuelled speculation that a Union cabinet reshuffle could be on the cards.Under Article 75(5) of the Constitution, a minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament for six consecutive months must cease to hold office. With Puri and Verma's Rajya Sabha terms ending on November 25, their omission from the UP list raises questions over whether the two will be given another route into Parliament or whether the BJP is preparing for a wider reshuffle. The party, however, has not indicated what the move means for either minister.Also beyond Uttar Pradesh, the BJP on Sunday named Dinesh Arya for the Uttarakhand seat and Trinamool Congress (TMC) defector Rukmini "Koel" Mallick for the West Bengal bypoll. In the March round of Rajya Sabha elections, it fielded its unit chiefs in Bihar and Odisha and retained one sitting MP in Odisha.
Article Summary: BJP names eight candidates for the Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh. All of its outgoing members from the state are dropped. Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma also are among those who have not been renominated. Voting for 10 UP seats is on October 16, and the last date for filing nominations is October 6.

Article Title: Lakhimpur Kheri case: UP changes public prosecutor; Supreme Court asks Allahabad High Court chief justice to decide on trial judge
Article Text:
SC seeks report from Allahabad HC

If doubts cast, better to replace PP: UP counsel

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh government informed Supreme Court on Monday that it has decided to replace the public prosecutor in the 2021 case of farmers being mowed down in Lakhimpur Kheri, but said allegations against the outgoing PP by the witness were unfounded. Former minister Ajay Mishra's son Ashish is an accused in the case.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also forwarded the vigilance report on the trial judge, placed before it in a sealed cover, to the Allahabad HC chief justice for appropriate decision. The witness had accused the judge of improperly withdrawing to himself cases under NDPS and SC/ST Act and acquitting the accused.UP standing counsel Ruchira Goel said the earlier PP was a seasoned prosecutor of 16 years and had not given up key witnesses as alleged.She said there were certain witnesses who had died and others had turned hostile, which he had given up. The bench said it understood the predicament but said whenever doubts were cast on the PP which would affect a free and fair trial, it was better to replace him.“We are not casting any aspersion on the professional ability of the earlier PP,” the bench said.Appearing for Mishra, senior advocate Siddharth Dave accused the witness of attempting to prejudice the trial, the PP and the trial judge by making wild allegations and trying to coerce them to record a conviction.“Every now and then, the witness threatens the trial judge and the PP by stating that he will complain to SC,” he said.The bench said the state had done a commendable job by replacing the PP but clarified, “We are not saying anything against anyone. Our only concern is that the trial should proceed smoothly in a free and fair manner.” The bench, which is monitoring progress of the trial, was informed that 86 of 131 witnesses in the case had been examined.The SC posted further hearing after two weeks.The case relates to an Oct 2021 incident when Ashish Mishra allegedly ran over protesting farmers with his SUV, killing four of them. A mob of farmers then lynched the driver of the vehicle and two BJP workers. A journalist was also killed in the violence. Ashish is on bail and is barred from residing in his hometown Lakhimpur Kheri.UP standing counsel Ruchira Goel said the earlier PP was a seasoned prosecutor of 16 years and had not given up key witnesses as alleged.
Article Summary: Supreme Court to replace public prosecutor in 2021 case of farmers being mowed down in Lakhimpur Kheri. Former minister Ajay Mishra's son Ashish is an accused in the case. The witness had accused the judge of improperly withdrawing to himself cases under NDPS and SC/ST Act.

Article Title: Probe sex assault case against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad, court directs Delhi cops

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has issued a notice to DCP, IGI airport, directing that an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad be completed and the report be filed by the next date of hearing, after rejecting Delhi Police 's request for more time.The court of additional chief judicial magistrate Neha Mittal listed the matter for further hearing on Oct 23.The complainant has accused Azad of raping her on the pretext of marriage.Alleging that police failed to register an FIR, she had approached the court seeking a direction for registration of a case against Azad.During earlier proceedings, the court issued a notice to Delhi Police and asked for a status report. Police submitted a status report detailing the progress of the inquiry conducted so far. However, they sought an additional two to three months to conclude the preliminary probe. The complainant opposed the police plea for more time.The judge noted in the order that "since the offence alleged in the present application is punishable with life imprisonment, section 173(3) BNSS does not apply and hence, there is no scope for conducting preliminary inquiry".Section 173(3) allows police to conduct a preliminary inquiry before registering an FIR for offences that carry a jail term of three to under seven years.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has issued a notice to DCP, IGI airport, directing that an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad be completed. The complainant has accused Azad of raping her on the pretext of marriage. Delhi Police sought an additional two to three months to conclude the preliminary probe.

Article Title: Rajya Sabha polls: 8 fresh BJP faces for UP, Hardeep Puri among 2 ministers dropped
Article Text:

Whether BJP deploys Puri for Punjab polls remains to be seen

NEW DELHI: BJP on Monday did not renominate two Union ministers, Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, as its Rajya Sabha picks from Uttar Pradesh, rekindling speculation that PM Narendra Modi is looking to reshuffle his council of ministers as vacancies rise.Two other ministers, Ravneet Singh Bittu and George Kurien, were similarly left out of Rajya Sabha nominations in June, leading to their resignation. While these two were state ministers, a position held by Verma as well, Puri is a Cabinet minister holding the crucial portfolio of petroleum and natural gas.His likely exit from the Cabinet after the then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan quit in July following CJP's stir over paper leaks further makes the case of a reshuffle as both are demanding portfolios. Consumer affairs, food and public distribution minister Pralhad Joshi is currently handling the education ministry as an additional charge.A minister since Sep 2017, former diplomat Puri is the lone Sikh face in the council of ministers and had unsuccessfully contested the Lok Sabha election from Amritsar in 2019.Some Union ministers like Pankaj Chaudhary and Harsh Malhotra, now heading BJP’s state units in UP and Delhi respectively, have been given organisation responsibilities in an indication that their continuation in govt is unlikely to continue beyond the expected reshuffle.Puri’s term as Rajya Sabha MP from UP ends in Nov, and rules allow a minister to hold his office for six months without being an MP. Not having much of a political constituency of his own, it remains to be seen if he, like Bittu, will be deployed in the Punjab assembly polls, scheduled to be held along with four other states, including UP, early next year.While the impending Punjab election was cited by some experts as a case for his continuation due to his Sikh background, BJP brass in the end chose to not repeat any of its RS candidates, a practice it had followed in the last round of elections as well.Since taking over as PM in 2014, Modi has gone for an overhaul of his council of ministers before the mid-term in both his earlier stints, giving rise to the prospect of a major rejig as his govt is now well into its third year in its third stint.
Article Summary: Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma not renominated as Rajya Sabha picks from Uttar Pradesh. Two other ministers, Ravneet Singh Bittu and George Kurien, were similarly left out in June. Puri is a Cabinet minister holding the crucial portfolio of petroleum and natural gas.

Article Title: 'Story matters, so does how you get it': Delhi Police lays down rules for scribes covering protests
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Monday issued an advisory for journalists covering protests, asking them to carry valid identity cards and ensure that their presence or activities do not obstruct police operations or the movement of law enforcement personnel.In a social media post on X, Delhi Police issued the guidelines for journalists and said, "The story matters, so does how you get it!""All journalists assigned to cover protests are advised to carry valid identity cards issued by their respective organisations and/or valid PIB/DIP accreditation cards," the guidelines read."They should keep their identification cards visibly displayed at all times to facilitate identification by law enforcement agencies present at the site. They should also ensure that their presence or activities do not obstruct police operations or the movement of law enforcement personnel," it added."During tense situations, journalists present at the site should maintain a reasonable and safe distance while covering and recording the proceedings. They should position themselves in a manner that clearly distinguishes them from protestors," it further said.This comes days after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment during Saturday's protest against the Election Commission at Jantar Mantar.Delhi Police received the complaints and forwarded them to the Crime Branch for further inquiry.On Sunday, Delhi Police, on its official X handle, said that during the October 3 protest in the New Delhi area, which sparked a "law and order situation", allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. "New Delhi District has received their complaints and the same are transferred to Crime Branch for fair and impartial enquiry."Following the allegations, several independent journalists held a protest outside Parliament Street police station, demanding FIRs against the officers.
Article Summary: Delhi Police issues guidelines for journalists covering protests. It asks them to carry valid identity cards and ensure that their presence or activities do not obstruct police operations or the movement of law enforcement personnel. This comes days after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment.

Article Title: Bypolls in 5 assembly constituencies, 1 Lok Sabha seat tomorrow: Key contests to watch

Will Vijay’s ‘magic’ charm Tamil Nadu again

Thattanchavady: NDA's popularity test in Puducherry

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) will conduct byelections on Tuesday for five assembly seats and one Lok Sabha constituency across three states and the Union territory of Puducherry, with vote counting scheduled for Friday.The constituencies going to the polls are Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu, Thattanchavady in Puducherry, Rejinagar and Nandigram in West Bengal, and Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in Assam.The bypolls come amid growing scrutiny of the Election Commission (EC) over reported differences between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The Indian Express reported last month that Sandhu and Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge.The report triggered protests seeking Kumar’s resignation, even as the EC maintained that all decisions had been taken unanimously by the CEC and the Election Commissioners. The issue has also reached the Supreme Court, which took up a petition seeking Kumar's removal, and issued notices to the EC and the Centre.However, the Chief Justice Surya Kant-led bench declined to pass an interim order, observing that it could not do so based solely on a media report whose accuracy remained uncertain.The bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram will be the first major electoral test for chief minister C Joseph Vijay since his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) came to power following the April assembly elections, just two years after the party was launched. A total of 27 candidates are contesting in Madurantakam, while 30 are in the fray in Dharapuram.The vacancies arose after AIADMK MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel of Madurantakam and P Sathyabama of Dharapuram resigned from their seats. Both subsequently joined TVK and have been fielded by the party in the bypolls.The DMK, led by former chief minister MK Stalin, as well as the AIADMK and CPI, have also fielded candidates. The CPI is among the parties that supported TVK after it emerged as the single-largest party, paving the way for it to form the government.In West Bengal, the focus is on Nandigram, which fell vacant after Suvendu Adhikari, now the BJP’s first chief minister in the state, resigned as its MLA. Adhikari defeated Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur and retained his Nandigram stronghold in the April assembly elections. He chose to represent Bhabanipur, vacating Nandigram and necessitating the bypoll. The BJP has fielded Hasirani Rath, whose son Chandranath, an aide of Adhikari, was shot dead days after the assembly election results were announced.The TMC, which was voted out after 15 years and has since split into two factions, decided not to field a candidate after its original nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the contest. It instead extended support to the Congress. However, in a twist, Congress candidate Milan Pradhan was arrested hours later in connection with a 2007 case. On September 29, the Calcutta high court granted him interim bail till October 21, while the Supreme Court adjourned the West Bengal government’s plea challenging the order, paving the way for Pradhan to contest the bypoll.The rival TMC faction is also in the fray, having nominated Mohammad Eteshamul Haque, while the CPI has fielded Santigopal Giri.The other seat, Rejinagar, fell vacant after Humayun Kabir resigned as MLA. Kabir had earlier formed his own Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) after being suspended and subsequently expelled by the TMC. He also won the Nowda seat and chose to represent it, prompting him to field his son, Golam Nabi Azad, from Rejinagar, where around 70% of voters belong to the minority community.The BJP has fielded Sakharav Sarkar, while the CPI(M) has nominated Syed Asad Ali. The Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction has fielded Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, while the rival faction has nominated Safiuzzaman Sheikh. The Congress candidate is Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi.In Assam, the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of then-Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi, who switched to the BJP in April ahead of the assembly elections, which the saffron party won, securing a third straight term. The contest is significant for the Congress, which held the seat after Bordoloi won it in 2019 and 2024. The party has fielded former MLA Sibamoni Bora, while the BJP has nominated Devasish Sharma.AIUDF president Badruddin Ajmal is also contesting after replacing the party’s original nominee, Rejaul Karim Sarkar. With more than 55% of Nagaon’s voters belonging to the minority community, the contest among the BJP, Congress and AIUDF is being closely watched, despite 15 candidates being in the fray.The Thattanchavady bypoll is being seen as a test of the four-month-old NDA government led by chief minister N Rangasamy. The seat fell vacant after Rangasamy, who won both Thattanchavady and Mangalam in the April assembly elections, kept Mangalam.The All India NR Congress, which leads the NDA government, has fielded Ashok Anand, while the DMK and Congress have nominated K Sethu Selvam and E Vinayagam, respectively. The Congress has the backing of its Tamil Nadu ally TVK. Eleven candidates are in the fray.
Article Summary: Election Commission to conduct byelections on Tuesday for five assembly seats and one Lok Sabha constituency. constituencies going to the polls are Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu, Thattanchavady in Puducherry, Rejinagar and Nandigram in West Bengal, and Nagaon in Assam. Vote counting scheduled for Friday.

Article Title: 'Misled the public': BJP rejects Rahul Gandhi’s 'illegal' claims on Form 6 and SIR
Article Text:
What is Form 6

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday came down heavily on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and accused him of misleading the public over the Supreme Court's observation on Form 6 and the Election Commission's decision on the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra compared Rahul's claims to the Congress leader's earlier statements on the Rafale issue."Rahul Gandhi misled the public on two counts. First, he claimed that Form 6 was illegal - specifically mentioning the Bharatiya Janata Party in this context. However, the Court did not declare Form 6 illegal today. It noted that the petition mentioned a modification to Form 6, so the Court said it would look into the matter," Patra said."We had not consented to any such modification. If any modification has indeed taken place, that will become clear only after a notice is issued. Yet, when we read the detailed order and look at the Election Commission's press release dated September 26, 2026, it becomes evident that the Commission had clearly stated there were no changes to Form 6 and that the Supreme Court had validated the declaration form attached to it," he said.This comes hours after Rahul Gandhi alleged that the CEC had changed Form 6 "illegally and unilaterally", citing the Supreme Court's observation which came earlier in the day."It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP," Rahul said."He and everyone else involved in this criminal assault on our democracy will be held accountable," he added.The Congress leader also shared a screenshot of the September 26 Election Commission statement which read: "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used."In its response, the EC said the order for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar, issued on June 24, 2025, had received the unanimous approval of the Commission and was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court in its judgment dated May 27, 2026.EC officials also clarified that Form 6 itself had not been changed, but that a declaration had been attached to the form under the Bihar SIR order, as quoted by PTI.This came after the Supreme Court said it had not approved any modification to Form 6 used by the EC during the SIR exercise in various states."Any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When records are produced, we would like to see who has modified it," a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said.Form 6 is the application used by eligible voters for inclusion in the electoral roll.The declaration was attached to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR, which began with the EC's June 24, 2025, order. The declaration sought additional details, including information about the applicant's parents.According to EC officials, the form itself remained unchanged, while the declaration was a separate document attached to it for the SIR exercise. Outside SIR, the forms prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, apply.The declaration was later withdrawn from the EC's online portals.The online version of Form 6 and the declaration also used a single OTP for both, rather than requiring separate OTP verification, which had led to suggestions that the declaration was part of Form 6.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra compared Rahul's claims to the Congress leader's earlier statements on the Rafale issue. This comes hours after Rahul Gandhi alleged that the CEC had changed Form 6 "illegally and unilaterally", citing the Supreme Court's observation which came earlier in the day.

Article Title: ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’: Congress announces nationwide campaign against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

NEW DELHI: Hours after the Supreme Court clarified that it had not approved any modified version of Form 6, Congress on Monday announced an intensified nationwide campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Party's general secretary KC Venugopal threatened that the agitation over alleged “vote theft” would continue until Kumar is removed and the electoral system is corrected.Announcing the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign, Venugopal said the Congress would take its protest from blocks and villages to the national capital, with marches, chaupals, rallies and a major mobilisation in Delhi planned between October 10 and November 26.“Congress President has given a clear direction today to the PCC Presidents, In-charges, and General Secretaries for an aggressive, nationwide campaign against vote theft - 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao'. This is the slogan we are raising,” he said.The announcement came after a meeting of Congress general secretaries, in-charges, PCC presidents and frontal organisation heads chaired by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and attended by leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.Venugopal said the campaign would not be a short-term protest. “Rahul Gandhi has also given clear directions to our leaders that this agitation is not going to end tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. This will be a continuous, aggressive campaign till Gyanesh Kumar is removed and the system has to be corrected,” he said.The Supreme Court on Monday said it had not approved any modified Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters during the SIR. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When the record is produced, we would like to see who has modified.”Venugopal seized on the development to attack the Election Commission. “You know the Election Commission has become the 'Cheating Commission of India'. After this much - after this much observation from the Supreme Court and the opposition parties, and two Commissioners' remarks also, he is misleading the people,” he said.The first phase of the Congress campaign, from October 10 to 20, will feature block-level bike rallies, cycle rallies and padyatras. “All over India, it will happen. Thousands of workers in each block will participate in this march demanding this thing, and we will burn the effigies of Gyanesh Kumar,” Venugopal said.From October 25 to November 25, Congress workers, whom the party is calling “Vote Rakshaks”, will hold village chaupals and identify voters it alleges have been unfairly deleted from electoral rolls.The campaign will culminate with a mega rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 and six ‘Chalo Delhi’ yatras on November 25 and 26.Venugopal also announced a protest march from Parliament to the Election Commission on Tuesday, saying, “Our aim is to have a peaceful demonstration to show the protest against the Election Commission of India .”“Every person of India wants to remove the Chief Election Commissioner. Only two people want to retain him - Prime Minister and Amit Shah,” he said.

Supreme Court on Monday said it had not approved any modified Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters during the SIR. Party's general secretary KC Venugopal threatened that the agitation would continue until Kumar is removed and the electoral system is corrected.

NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders stepped up attacks on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Monday after the Supreme Court clarified that it had not approved modifications to Form 6 being used by the Election Commission of India (ECI) during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The INDIA bloc is set to hold a protest march from Parliament House to the Election Commission on Tuesday, with opposition parties demanding accountability over the SIR exercise and raising questions about the functioning of the poll panel. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the Supreme Court's clarification showed that Kumar had changed Form 6 “illegally and unilaterally”.“It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP,” Gandhi posted on X.He said the CEC and others involved in what he called a “criminal assault on democracy” would be held accountable.Congress leader Pawan Khera said the ECI's earlier justification for the modified Form 6 had now been contradicted by the Supreme Court.“The ECI had sought to justify the controversial Form 6 declaration by claiming that the Form 6 had been upheld by the Supreme Court.That claim has now been squarely contradicted by the Court itself,” Khera said.Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Dharmendra Yadav alleged that no election had been fair under Kumar's supervision and questioned the conduct of polls in several states.“Under their supervision, has any election ever been fair? You tell me, weren't questions raised in Bengal? You tell me, weren't questions raised in Bihar? Weren't questions raised in Delhi? Or didn't the people of Maharashtra raise questions? Didn't the people of Haryana raise questions?” Yadav said.He claimed that five SP seats were “defeated in counting” during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and said the party's performance was not a “favour” from Kumar.“If there hadn't been cheating, 43 Samajwadi Party candidates would have won alone, and our alliance would have won nearly 48 seats,” he alleged.Yadav also said opposition parties would continue their campaign until Kumar resigned.“All those who believe in democracy... such people will make Gyanesh Gupta resign, no matter how many ways of struggle are required, it will be done,” he said.AAP leader Manish Sisodia also targeted Kumar over the Form 6 changes.“The Supreme Court has clearly said Gyanesh Kumar did not get permission to change Form 6,” Sisodia said, alleging that the clarification raised questions over how the changes were made.Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Anil Desai said concerns surrounding the SIR had not been adequately addressed. “Several issues have come to light regarding the SIR, and none of the points raised have been refuted,” Desai said.He alleged that the deletion of voters' names in Maharashtra had caused anxiety and demanded accountability.“The Chief Election Commissioner should accept responsibility for the errors that have come to light and resign. That is why the protest march is taking place tomorrow,” he said.RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav announced an “Akrosh March” at block levels across Bihar on October 7, followed by district-level demonstrations and a march towards the Lok Bhavan on October 8.MAITC MP Derek O’Brien said: “In 2023, a record 146 MPs were unilaterally suspended from Parliament, so BJP could bulldoze CEC Bill which replaced Chief Justice (with a Union Minister) from Selection Committee of CEC & ECs!”“Tuesday, 146+ MPs march in protest from Parliament to EC. GK must GO,” he posted.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us.”The court was hearing a PIL concerning alleged unilateral decisions related to the SIR. It issued notices to the ECI and Centre but did not pass an interim order restraining Kumar from taking decisions.The opposition's planned march on Tuesday is expected to intensify the political pressure on the poll panel, while the Supreme Court proceedings will determine how the disputed SIR decisions and Form 6 modifications are examined further.
